dataset.title: Philippines_GIS_stream_network_n128
dataset.methodNote: The network was derived from a nationwide 2013 IfSAR DEM; the source paper reports 5 m resolution and 1 m vertical RMSE. It is a modelled hydrology network, not a field-surveyed named-waterbody boundary.

stationCrosscheck.officialSource: DENR-EMB CALABARZON updated waterbodies table; coordinates were read from the indexed source and not copied into this artifact.
stationCrosscheck.calculation: Transform source DMS station locations to EPSG:3857 and calculate the nearest Euclidean point-to-polyline distance against source network line features.

networkTopology.interpretation: The two EMB station clusters are close to adjacent, connected segments in the same modelled Marikina_Pasig catchment network. This supports a hydrological continuity candidate, but does not establish that the separately named adopted stretches are the same official waterbody or define its full extent.

limitations: Stream-network lines are modelled from a 2013 elevation dataset and are a candidate cross-check only.
Distances were measured to station locations in source metadata; the station coordinate values are not redistributed here.
A connected modelled network is not an authoritative name crosswalk, a verified full-channel trace, or a fishing-access or legal-status determination.
No fish survey, salinity profile, current water-quality result, or permission to fish was established by this spatial crosscheck.
nextAction: Obtain an authorized official station-to-channel crosswalk or independently validated hydrography trace before resolving Tagbac creek and Tagbac River names or publishing any geometry.
